By this application, the applicant is seeking the relief of pre- arrest bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C."), as he apprehends arrest in connection with Crime Register No.129 of 2022 registered with Alibaug Police Station, Raigad.

The offences alleged against him are punishable under Sections 328, 272, 273, 188 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC"), and also under Sections 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 26(2)(iv), 26(3),
30(2)(a), and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution, the informant, one Vishwajit Vithhal Shinde, who is a Food Inspector,
conducted a series of raids on 31 May 2022 along with his team and a panch witness.
The first raid was carried out at around 4:30 p.m. at M/s Ashoka Pan Stall, 903-aba-1891-2022.doc Alibaug.
The second raid followed at about 5:20 p.m. at M/s Rupa Pan Shop, Alibaug.
The third raid was conducted at about 6:10 p.m. at M/s I Love Alibaug Pan Shop, Alibaug.
During these raids, the team seized prohibited and banned substances such as Vimal Pan Masala, scented tobacco, Manikchand Gutkha, and Kesaryukt Goa.
Based on these seizures, an FIR was lodged against the present applicant, alleging his involvement in the storage and sale of such contraband.
3. The learned Advocate appearing for the applicant submitted that the applicant has extended full co-operation during the course of investigation.
It is pointed out that the charge-sheet has already been filed, which shows that the investigation is complete.
It is further submitted that this Court had granted interim protection by its order dated 13 July 2022.
The said protection has been continued from time to time and is still operative.
The applicant has scrupulously abided by the conditions imposed by this Court while granting ad-interim protection and has not misused the liberty granted.
On these grounds, it is prayed that the interim relief granted earlier be confirmed and continued.
4. On the other hand, the learned APP opposed the application.
It is argued that the material collected during investigation prima facie indicates the applicant's involvement in the alleged offences.
It is therefore submitted that this is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail and the application deserves rejection.
5. I have carefully considered the submissions of both sides.
On perusal of the interim order dated 13 July 2022, it is clear that this 903-aba-1891-2022.doc Court had granted interim protection to the applicant, subject to conditions.
The record shows that the applicant has co-operated with the investigation.
The prosecution has now filed the charge- sheet, which means custodial interrogation of the applicant is no longer necessary.
The interim order has remained in operation for more than two years, and during this period, no breach of conditions by the applicant has been reported.
In such circumstances, there is no justification to recall the protection which has already been enjoyed without any misuse.

6. Therefore, considering the settled principles that anticipatory bail can be confirmed if the applicant has cooperated with the investigation, charge-sheet is filed, and interim protection has been in force without misuse, I am of the view that the applicant has made out a case for confirmation of interim relief.
7. Accordingly, the interim protection granted to the applicant vide order dated 13 July 2022 stands confirmed.
The same shall continue to remain in force, subject to the terms and conditions already imposed therein.

8. Hence, following order:
a) In the event of arrest in connection with Crime Register No.129 of 2022 registered with Alibaug police station, Raigad, the applicant be released on bail on furnishing Naresh Pandurang Mhatre vs State Of Maharashtra on 17 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185105162/
2 P.R. bond of Rs.25,000/-, along with one or two sureties in the like amount.

sentences.text: b) The applicant shall co-operate with the investigation and report to the Investigating Officer as and when directed.

903-aba-1891-2022.doc c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer.

d) The applicant shall not obstruct or hamper the police investigation and not to play mischief with the evidence collected or yet to be collected by the police.
e) The applicant shall, at the time of execution of the bond, furnish his address and mobile number to the investigating officer, and the Court concerned, and shall not change the residence till the final disposal of the case.
9. The Anticipatory Bail Application stands disposed of in above terms.
